Outage Restoration SLA: The Contractor shall guarantee restoration of major network outages (defined as an outage affecting more than 10% of residents in any single building, or a complete building outage) within six (6) hours of notification. COR Responsibilities: The Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) is responsible for quality assurance and contract oversight. The COR’s role is strictly surveillance, verification of contract compliance, and escalation of unresolved issues to the CO. 2.7.1 Invoicing and Resident Billing Restrictions The contractor will submit a single, consolidated monthly itemized (by building) invoice after installation for Wi-Fi to the Government. The Government will send a cure notice to the Contractor, unless the reason for the termination is late delivery. Kui hankemenetlusest kõrvaldamise alus esineb, võib ettevõtja soovi korral esitada tõendeid selle kohta, et ta on võtnud meetmeid oma usaldusväärsuse taastamiseks. This Statement of Work (SOW) outlines the responsibilities of contractor chosen for the supply and installation of two each, air compressors, air dryer and oil water separator. It’s also for the removal and haul away of 2 each air compressor at 3640 Patrick Avenue, Joint Base Andrews. This project includes the replacement of the existing Ingersoll Rand 30 hp rotary screw compressors (2 each), refrigerated air dryer, and oil-wate

for the removal and haul away of 2 each air compressor at 3640 Patrick Avenue, Joint Base Andrews. This project includes the replacement of the existing Ingersoll Rand 30 hp rotary screw compressors (2 each), refrigerated air dryer, and oil-water separator with two each of the same spec air compressor, air dryer and oil-water separator. This will include all the piping needed to connect the two air compressors, air dryer and oil-water separator to the existing piping to disperse the air through the building. 1.2.2. The two Quincy QGD-30 or equivalent air compressors will provide a reliable and continuous source of high-pressure, high-volume compressed air, which is critical for all pneumatic operations within the aircraft structural maintenance shop. They will replace our current, failing system, which consists of one inoperable unit and one that consistently overheats, causing severe operational delays. This new system is expected to eliminate work stoppages and significantly improve the efficiency of critical maintenance tasks such as sandblasting, painting, sanding, and operating various pneumatic hand tools. The continuous-duty rating and robust cooling will ensure the compressors can meet our high operational tempo without failure. This directly supports our missio
